method: Ranked by claude-sonnet-5-5, which read 10 of 14 shortlisted pieces

picks.title: Network Researchers Nail Down Theory of ‘Perfect Resilience’
picks.author: Ben Brubaker
picks.why_it_matters: Graph-minor theory plus the Robertson-Seymour theorem pins down exactly four network structures that defeat perfect resilience in local routing, a clean result on a real engineering problem.

picks.title: Collections: On the ‘Sullan Republic’
picks.source: A Collection of Unmitigated Pedantry (Bret Devereaux)
picks.author: Bret Devereaux
picks.why_it_matters: Argues Sulla did not save the Roman Republic but buried it and built a weaker substitute that collapsed within a generation, a sharp reframing of the period.

picks.title: Language Models Can Rewrite Their Own Weights
picks.author: lwhsiao
picks.why_it_matters: A 27B model edits its own weights using only forward passes and improves on unseen problems. The claim is bold and the scale-dependence result is worth checking.

picks.title: Decoding base64 email attachments: a speed ranking of programming languages
picks.author: Daniel Lemire
picks.why_it_matters: Shows how simdutf strips base64 line breaks inside its SIMD loop, giving a 30x spread across languages and a 28x speedup for PHP.

picks.title: Detonating A Huge Pile of Lead Azide. Really.
picks.why_it_matters: A chemist explains what makes lead azide a sensitive primary explosive and why the Army's planned mass detonation is such an unusual event.
